subject: Request: Exec approval for OptiHealth liability & indemnity variance
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Tanya Kapoor <tanya.kapoor@optihealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Exec approval for OptiHealth liability & indemnity variance

Tanya — attaching the latest redlines and SOW after today's product/finance sync. OptiHealth is asking for two material contract changes we need executive sign-off on: (1) liability cap increase to $5,000,000 (from our standard $1,000,000) and (2) a broader indemnity carve-out for third‑party IP claims that shifts more risk to Redwood.

Attachments: Redlines_OptiHealth_v3.docx, SOW_OptiHealth_vFinal.pdf

Quick summary of ask and why: 
- OptiHealth (large payer platform) is requesting the higher cap to cover potential downstream claims tied to clinical integrations. They are also insisting on a customer-favorable indemnity for third‑party claims originating from their data suppliers.
- Commercial asks: they expect 10–15% discount tied to a 24‑month committed usage.

Marissa / Laura — tagging you to confirm legal stance and recommended escalation steps. Tanya — I’ll loop back after internal approval. If you have a preferred timeline for signature, flag it here.

Thanks,
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0193
From: Tanya Kapoor <tanya.kapoor@optihealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: OptiHealth Legal <legal@optihealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 18:10:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exec approval for OptiHealth liability & indemnity variance

Sean — thanks for sending. Appreciate the transparency. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The $5M cap is non-negotiable given the potential exposure from downstream clinical partners; $1M leaves material residual risk.
- On indemnity: we need Redwood to indemnify OptiHealth for third‑party claims only to the extent caused by Redwood's willful misconduct or breach of warranty. We cannot accept broad vendor indemnities that capture our supply chain.
- Timeline: we are targeting a July 1 production integration, so hoping to execute an agreement by end of August.

We can consider commercial tradeoffs (e.g., annual commitment + extended term) to bridge economics. Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow if it helps.

Tanya
VP, Strategic Partnerships | OptiHealth
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: Exec approval for OptiHealth liability & indemnity variance

Team — quick read on OptiHealth's counter: 
- They will not accept $1M cap; pushing for $5M. They tied this to their integrations and vendor obligations.
- Indemnity ask narrows Redwood's ability to rely on mutuality; they want indemnity limited to Redwood-caused claims but with broad discovery language.

Recommendation: escalate to Exec/Deal Desk for approval to (A) accept a $5M cap for this strategic payer account only, limited to direct damages, carve out consequential and punitive damages; (B) accept indemnity language that is Redwood-liability-limited (no responsibilities for customer supply chain), but require additional contractual safeguards: stronger SLA credits, enhanced logging, and a monthly security report during onboarding.

Commercial offset idea from sales: one-time 10% onboarding credit + 18-month minimum commitment to mitigate unit economics.

If Legal (Laura) signs off on wording, we should present a concise approval request to the Exec (CTO/CRO) this morning.

Marissa
Senior Deal Desk Manager
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 11:23:45 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: Exec approval for OptiHealth liability & indemnity variance

Summary of legal position and proposed carve: 
- Liability cap: consenting to $5M cap for OptiHealth is acceptable as an exception given strategic value, provided the cap is limited to direct, provable damages and excludes consequential, punitive, and loss-of-public-trust clauses. Add a combined single-claim carve so the cap isn't re-set per incident.
- Indemnity: we should accept the customer's wording only if we insert: (i) limitation that Redwood's indemnity applies only to claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (ii) carve out any indemnity for the customer's upstream vendors; (iii) require that OptiHealth pursue indemnification from their suppliers first (flow-down obligation).
- Controls: require additional security attestations during onboarding (SOC 2 snapshot + network segmentation confirmation) and a 30-day onboarding SLA credit if integration milestones slip.

Draft language: see attached Redlines_OptiHealth_v3.docx (redline highlights on p.3–5).

Please approve the following ask to Exec: Approve an exception to standard cap up to $5M (direct damages only) and accept narrowed indemnity (Redwood liability limited to gross negligence/willful misconduct) in exchange for a one-time 10% onboarding credit and an 18-month committed term.

Laura
Director, Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: Exec approval for OptiHealth liability & indemnity variance

Thanks — I support escalating. A couple of commercial guardrails before we present to the exec team: 
- Approve $5M cap for direct damages only. No change to warranty language beyond what Laura proposed.
- Approve one-time 10% onboarding credit (applied to month 1 invoice) conditioned on 18-month minimum commitment.
- Require a technical onboarding checklist (logging + SOC 2 snapshot) and a post-integration review at 90 days with the customer success team.

I will present this for final sign-off to the CRO and CFO this afternoon. If anyone expects material opposition, flag now.

-Aditya
VP, Revenue Operations
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Tanya Kapoor <tanya.kapoor@optihealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Final: Exec approval for OptiHealth liability & indemnity variance — next steps

Tanya — good news: management has approved a one-time exception for OptiHealth under the following conditions: 
- Liability cap increased to $5,000,000, limited to direct damages only (no consequential, punitive, or reputational damages).
- Redwood's indemnity narrowed: Redwood will indemnify OptiHealth only for claims resulting from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct; OptiHealth must pursue upstream vendor indemnity first.
- Commercial offset: one-time 10% onboarding credit (applies to first invoice) in exchange for an 18-month committed usage term.
- Controls: SOC 2 snapshot and onboarding logging checklist must be completed prior to go‑live; a 90‑day post-integration review will follow.

I have attached the finalized redline (Redlines_OptiHealth_v3.docx) and SOW for signature. Please review and let me know if we should route the redlined doc through DocuSign (link attached) or your internal e-sign flow.

Thanks for working through this — if you want a short execution call I can make time today.

Best,
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
